title: 1934 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship

{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland | year = 1934 | image = | dates = 6 May – 30 September 1934 | teams = 12 | connacht = | munster = Limerick | leinster = Dublin | ulster = | matches = 13 | poty = | team = Limerick | titles = 4th | captain = [[Timmy Ryan]] | manager = | team2 = Dublin | captain2 = [[Stephen Feeny]] | manager2 = | totalgoals = 95 (7.30 per game) | totalpoints = 105 (8.07 per game) | topscorer = [[Dave Clohessey]] (8–2) | previous = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1933|1933]] | next = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1935|1935]] }} The '''All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1934''' was the 48th series of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], [[Ireland]]'s premier [[hurling]] [[single-elimination tournament|knock-out competition]]. [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] won the championship, beating [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] 5–2 to 2–6 in a replay of the [[1934 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].{{cite web|url=http://gaaweb.sitesuite.cn/page/roll_of_honour2.html |title=All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Roll of Honour |publisher=The GAA website |access-date=22 July 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110905085701/http://gaaweb.sitesuite.cn/page/roll_of_honour2.html |archive-date=5 September 2011 }} ==Format== The All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship was run on a provincial basis as usual. All games were played on a knockout basis whereby once a team lost they were eliminated from the championship. The format for the All-Ireland series of games ran as follows: * The winners of the [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster Championship]] advanced directly to the All-Ireland final. * The winners of the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] advanced directly to a lone All-Ireland semi-final. * [[Galway GAA|Galway]], a team who faced no competition in the [[Connacht Senior Hurling Championship|Connacht Championship]], entered the championship at the All-Ireland semi-final stage where they played the Munster champions. * There were no representatives from the [[Ulster Senior Hurling Championship|Ulster Championship]] in the All-Ireland series. ==Results== ===[[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship]]=== {{footballbox |date=May 6, 1934

final, 2 September 1934'') ===Miscellaneous=== *On 3 June three-in-a-row hopefuls [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] set sail for the [[United States]] where they took part in a series of exhibition games. The team returned home on 14 July and resumed their participation on the [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster Championship]]. ==Golden Jubilee== The All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1934 marked the fiftieth anniversary of the foundation of the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]. *In honour of the [[golden jubilee]] a special set of All-Ireland medals were struck and presented to the championship winner, and a postage stamp was issued on 27 July 1934, which was designed by [[Richard King (artist)]].{{cite news |last=Hegarty |first=Fr Kevin |title=Richard King |work=Second Reading |publisher=[[The Mayo News]] |date=2009-03-19 |url=http://www.mayonews.ie/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=6151&Itemid=40 |access-date=2014-03-26 |archive-date=30 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330210903/http://www.mayonews.ie/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=6151&Itemid=40 |url-status=dead }}
"They were all delighted in Limerick over the G.A.A. Jubilee Stamp. They regard it as an omen that the colours chosen for the jersey of the hurler depicted on the stamp are those of the winners of the 1934 All-Ireland".''An Gaedheal'' 18 August 1934
